author: hywan
body:
This patch is the first part of the new `LatestEvents` API. It contains
the “framework”, i.e. the structure, tasks, logic to make it work, but
no latest events are computed for the moment.

The Latest Events API provides a lazy, reactive and efficient way to
compute the latest event for a room or a thread.

The latest event represents the last displayable and relevant event
a room or a thread has been received. It is usually displayed in a
_summary_, e.g. below the room title in a room list.

The entry point is `LatestEvents`. It is preferable to get a reference
to it from `Client::latest_events`, which already plugs everything to
build it. `LatestEvents` is using the `EventCache` and the `SendQueue`
to respectively get known remote events (i.e. synced from the server),
or local events (i.e. ones being sent).

## Laziness

`LatestEvents` is lazy, it means that, despite `LatestEvents` listening 
to all `EventCache` or `SendQueue` updates, it will
only do something if one is expected to get the latest event for a
particular room or a particular thread. Concretely, it means that
until `LatestEvents::listen_to_room` is called for a particular room, no
latest event will ever be computed for that room (and similarly with
`LatestEvents::listen_to_thread`).

If one is no longer interested to get the latest event for a
particular room or thread, the `LatestEvents::forget_room` and
`LatestEvents::forget_thread` methods must be used.

## Reactive

`LatestEvents` is designed to be reactive.
`LatestEvents::listen_and_subscribe_to_room` must be used, it
returns a `Subscriber`.

# PR Summary

Storage Factory Refactoring and Assets Service Implementation

## Overview

This PR refactors the storage implementation in the Grid system by replacing specific storage type fields with a polymorphic factory pattern. It also adds a new AssetsService endpoint for checking storage connections and changes S3 implementation from AWSS3IO to MinioS3IO.

## Change Types

| Type         | Description                            |
|--------------|----------------------------------------|
| Refactor     | Refactored storage implementation to use factory pattern |
| Enhancement  | Modified checkConnection() methods to enable method chaining |
| Feature      | Added new AssetsService endpoint for connection status |
| Enhancement  | Switched S3 implementation from AWSS3IO to MinioS3IO |

---

## Affected Modules

| Module / File          | Change Description                       |
|------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `GridStorage.java`     | Refactored to use polymorphic factory pattern instead of specific storage type fields |
| `Storage.java`         | Changed checkConnection() return type to enable method chaining |
| `*StorageFactory.java` | Updated implementations to return factory instance |
| `AssetsService.java`   | Added new service endpoint for checking asset storage connections |
| `MCP.java`             | Updated servlet references and added AssetsService |
| `WebMapping.java`      | Added user_id_s enum for storing user ID with crawls |
| `CrawlerDocument.java` | Renamed parameter from 'userId' to 'user_id' |

---

## Notes for Reviewers

* The storage implementation has been significantly refactored to use a factory pattern approach
* S3 implementation has been changed from AWSS3IO to MinioS3IO
* New AssetsService provides connection status information in JSON format

include security fixes and features by the peer dependencies for our users.

best experience.

We also don't need to open PRs anymore for our own minor and patch updates
that way. They will automatically be installed for users.

Graphql was installed as dev dependency in an old version, while it's unclear
why that was the case. I removed it as it was not required in the code.

author: volkmarglauche
body:
cfg_getfile is a user interface function. In addition, it currently implements a number of filename mangling tools, which are more or less useful in its own right. This pull request creates a helper function `cfg_getfile_cpath.m` which can be used without going through `spm_select` or `cfg_getfile`.

In addition, SPM has introduced `spm_file` as a collection of utility functions for filename handling. Most SPM code already uses `spm_file(..., 'CPath')` instead of `spm_select('CPath', ...)`. This pull request removes the remaining calls to `spm_select('CPath', ...)` and replaces them with calls to `spm_file(..., 'CPath')`.
